(1) Every woman has the right to:
a. live and maintain her life, as well as improve the standard of welfare in her life
b. practice religious teachings in accordance with Islamic sharia
c. obtain justice, security, and freedom to express opinions without discrimination
d. obtain protection of her person, family, honor, dignity and property rights
e. fulfill her basic needs to grow and develop properly, form a family and continue offspring

f. obtain fair and equal treatment in carrying out her roles and functions both in family life, society and participate fully in every process of making, determining and implementing development policies
g. obtain education and teaching at all types, levels, and pathways of education, without any obstacles and pressure in order to improve her skills and quality of life
h. receive information and knowledge for women about health, especially reproductive health comprehensively
column2: and i. obtain special protection in carrying out her work or profession against matters that threaten her safety and/or health related to reproductive function.

column1: (2) Every woman in her capacity as a wife, while in a marriage bond has the same rights and responsibilities as her husband over all matters relating to her marital life, relations with her children, and ownership and management of joint property in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

column1: ACEH BIREUEN,ACEH_BIREUEN.txt,5.1,NGO collaboration,stakeholder_engagement,No,Yes,0.0,1.0,false_positive,"CHAPTER VIII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 33
(1) The community may participate in the protection of women.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals and/or organizations.
(3) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) may be carried out by:
a. providing input and suggestions to the Regency Government related to policies, programs and activities for the protection of women
b. monitoring Regency Government policies related to the protection of women
c. initiating or proposing new policies that need to be established by the Regency Government in efforts to optimize the protection of women
d. assisting gampong apparatus in implementing efforts for the protection of women as regulated in this Qanun

CONCERNING THE EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, and basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals as well as between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women that causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.

Women have equal rights with men, however in certain discriminatory conditions, the government is obliged to implement affirmative action so that the rights of women and women in vulnerable groups need to receive protection so that they do not experience violence and can live decent lives in accordance with the principles of humanity, equality and justice.

The empowerment of women and protection of women is implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To carry out these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data.

The Regional Government of Bekasi City as the party that has the authority to regulate and protect the citizens of Bekasi City, deems it necessary to continuously carry out and formulate regulations in order to provide guarantees for the empowerment of women and protection of women in Bekasi City.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage security, psychological, physical, sexual, and economic well-being. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's territory.

Because the Indonesian government has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the elimination of all forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obligated to fulfill these provisions. The enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State.

Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the government recognizes the existence of children's rights. Human Rights inherent in children include, among others, basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

To fulfill the right to life, children require food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is provided to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children require space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (The best Interest of Child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of persecution, neglect, eviction and abuse by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House (Children protection home) or integrated service center for women and children (P2TP2A) for women and children victims of violence. A Safe House (shelter) is a safe place and is Friendly in nature for women and children.

The Integrated Service Center is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and is networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police.

The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of truth, justice, legal certainty, equality and upholding Human Rights.

From the above framework, the regional government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women. JAWA BARAT TASIKMALAYA,JAWA_BARAT_TASIKMALAYA.txt,4.2,Gender equality education,primary_prevention,No,Yes,0.0,1.0,false_positive,"CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya.
2. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Tasikmalaya.
3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in administering government affairs that are the authority of the Regency area.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.

9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.

10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

12. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.

15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere.
16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custody as a Parent over a Child.

18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Society is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations.

20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service.
21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area.

22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of Regional Government and society in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect.

23. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect.
24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
25. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims.

26. Accompaniment is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly.
29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children experiencing problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems

31. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.

32. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, Integrated Crisis Centers (PKT), Integrated Service Centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, Science and Technology Information Centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms.

33. Women and Child Protection Task Force is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Sub-district level.

34. Women and Child Protection Task Unit is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Village level.

35. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, society and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
36. Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is a coordinative institution at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.

37. Regional Action Plan for Child-Friendly Regency Development is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.","The policy defines women's protection as efforts aimed at fulfilling women's rights with the goal of achieving gender equality, indicating an explicit focus on women’s rights and gender equality as part of the policy framework.",Reference only

a. Who are suspected, alleged, charged, or sentenced for committing a criminal offense
b. Who become victims of a criminal offense or who see and/or hear directly the occurrence of a criminal offense.
Children in conflict with the law can also be defined as children who are forced to come into contact with the criminal justice system because:
a. They are suspected, charged, or declared proven guilty of violating the law
b. They have become victims as a result of acts of legal violations committed by person/group of persons/institution/state against them
c. They have seen, heard, felt, or known of an event of legal violation.
There are two categories of child behavior that cause them to come into conflict with the law:
a. Status Offence, namely child delinquent behavior which if committed by adults is not considered a crime, for example: skipping school, running away from home, etc.

b. Juvenile Delinquency, namely child delinquent behavior which if committed by adults is considered a crime or criminal act, for example: robbery, rape, sexual harassment, etc. Therefore, if viewed from its scope, children in conflict with the law can be divided into:

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sampang Regency.

2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the broadest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia
3. Regent is the Regent of Sampang.
4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sampang Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Governmental Affairs that are the authority of the Region.

6. The Office of Family Planning for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as DKBP3A, is a Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Sampang Regency.
7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb.

8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination

9. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights, so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination

10. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.

11. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
12. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
13. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
14. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

16. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
17. Victim is a woman including Female Workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such violence.
18. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.

19. Gender equality and justice is equal opportunity between men and women to participate in the development process, equal access to all forms of services, and have balanced social and economic status.

20. Integrated service is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of violence including criminal acts of human trafficking carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance
21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service institution for victims of violence against women and children

22. Protection of women is any act aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.

23. The system of women's empowerment and child protection is the entire process of implementing women's empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance up to - 6 - repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment

24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
25. Legal act is any act or action of a legal subject that has legal consequences and such legal consequences are indeed desired by the legal subject.
26. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred
27. Companion is a person who has expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
28. Social worker is a person who has expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the victim's psychology.
29. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process.
30. Women's Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence.

31. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved.
32. Standard Operational Procedure, hereinafter referred to as SOP, is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree.

33. column1: JAWA TIMUR SITUBONDO,JAWA_TIMUR_SITUBONDO.txt,6.3,Women workers,intersectional_approach,No,Yes,0.0,1.0,false_positive,"REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is organized based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection for a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which contradicts what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. To achieve integrated and comprehensive Protection services for Women and Children Victims of Violence, an integrated form of service from various related institutions is required, including medical services, medicolegal, psychosocial, legal assistance, accompaniment, economic independence (training). These services are carried out evenly across all levels of society so that every citizen has the right to obtain equal opportunities to receive security and legal protection.

In principle, the strategic target of implementing protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and safe and comfortable shelters that are conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

There are four important phenomena that need to be observed in relation to the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence. First, is violence against women and children from year to year the number is increasing with the mode of violence tending to be more sadistic (perpetrators who slit throats, pour hot water, throw into wells, to breaking parts of limbs and so on). Second, the many cases of violence against Domestic Workers (PRT) dominated by women that have occurred recently require attention from all parties, especially the existence of legal protection, regulations and policies that protect them. Third, the lack of facilities and infrastructure for safe and comfortable shelters that are conducive for victims of violence. These three phenomena indicate the increasing complexity of violent behavior whose victims are dominated by women and children, both those who work as domestic workers and others. Fourth, children are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in them is inherent dignity and worth as complete human beings. Children are the next generation of the nation's struggle ideals who have a strategic role, and have special characteristics and traits that are expected to ensure the continuity of the nation's and state's existence in the future. Children need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, cognitively, spiritually and socially.
Due to its nature, children's growth and development must be carried out in an environment that protects from all dangers in the form of optimal care.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and firmly giving a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence in Situbondo Regency is carried out based on Situbondo Regent Regulation Number 6 of 2006 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Acts of Violence against Women and Children and Situbondo Regent Decree No. 188/237 1P.00 L.2/2007 concerning the Integrated Service Center (PPT) for Victims of Violence against Women and Children in Situbondo Regency. As the phenomena described above, Regent Regulation Number 6 of 2006 has not been able to become a comprehensive legal umbrella in providing protection for women and children victims of violence. With the existence of this Regional Regulation, it is expected to anticipate and overcome the conditions of violence that occur in Situbondo Regency, so that it can provide protection and services to victims of violence in an integrated and comprehensive manner.","The policy text explicitly notes cases of violence against domestic workers dominated by women and highlights the need for legal protection, regulations, and policies to protect them, which constitutes a specific mention of women workers.",Reference only

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bengkayang Regency.
2. Regional Government is Bengkayang Regency as an element of regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Bengkayang Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age including a child still in the womb.

8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics that differ from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: blind, deaf, mentally disabled, physically disabled, socially maladjusted, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children.

9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect -5- children so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.

10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.

11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

13. Protection I is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.

15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.

16. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.

17. Violence is any act that results or will result in suffering and distress whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.

18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
21. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others.

23. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.

24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A for Protection of Women and Children is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by related agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.

27. Spiritual guidance is accompaniment in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved -7-.
28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children.
29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.

31. Accompaniment is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.

32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.

33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.","The policy explicitly references children who are trafficked within its definition of special protection, indicating trafficking is included.",Reference only

MALUKU UTARA TERNATE KOTA,MALUKU_UTARA_TERNATE_KOTA.txt,1.8,Human trafficking,scope_of_violence,No,Yes,0.0,1.0,false_positive,"CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Ternate.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor, and Regional Apparatus as elements of the administration of the Regional Government of the City of Ternate.
3. Regional Head is the Mayor of Ternate.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
6. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
7. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
8. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
10. Service is an action that must be immediately carried out to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.

11. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.

12. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in a Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico legal) psycho-social and legal services.
13. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.

15. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their child or father and his child and mother and her child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.

17. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins or other designations) and non-relatives (servants, drivers or other designations) who are present and reside in one house).
18. Implementation is a form of execution of protection for women and children victims of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions or other parties.

20. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a form of forum for women's empowerment and child protection based on the community in an effort to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, politics, law, protection and prevention of acts of violence and trafficking against women and children.","The policy text explicitly includes trafficking within the scope of prevention efforts referenced in the definition of P2TP2A, indicating human trafficking is addressed.",Reference only

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sikka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Sikka Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sikka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Sikka Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sikka Regency.
6. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit of the Regional Government of Sikka Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.

8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.

10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.

11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.

13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.

15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.

22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.

23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.

24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.

25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from the aspects of health, education and economic independence.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.","The policy defines victims to include women in conflict situations and post-conflict contexts, indicating the policy’s protection framework applies to women affected by conflict (and related emergency contexts).",Reference only

11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.

13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery.

15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

20. CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Palopo.
2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo.
3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government which is the authority of the autonomous region.

4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives Institution of Palopo City which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Palopo City.

6. Regional Agency is the Regional Apparatus of Palopo City which includes the Regional Secretariat, Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those still in the womb.

8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State.
9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence.

10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by regional government, family parties, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, society, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties.

11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of maltreatment and neglect.
12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.

13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery.
14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.

15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
17. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.

22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.

23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.

24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services for victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors.

25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from the aspects of health, education and economic independence.
26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
28. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

29. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.","The policy defines implementers as including customary institutions, indicating involvement/engagement with traditional/cultural organizations as part of implementation for victim recovery and related functions.",Reference only

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

3. Regional House of Representatives is the Regional People's Representative Institution as an Element of the Regional Government Administration of Poso Regency.
4. Child is a Person who has not yet reached 18 Years of age, including those in the womb.
5. Victim is a Woman and child who experiences violence and or threat of violence in conflict situations, post-conflict, domestic sphere and or public.
6. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services and Recovery for Victims of Violence.

7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the Government, Family Parties, Advocates, Social Institutions, Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Special Protection is Protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances (drugs), children victims of kidnapping sales trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of mistreatment and neglect.
9. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered both physically, psychologically and economically.
10. Implementer is Government Agencies and Social Institutions in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery.
11. Violence is any act and or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual, or neglect.
12. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or bodily defects to a person, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
13. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

15. Domestic Neglect is the act of neglecting a person within the household scope whereas according to the applicable law for the person concerned or because of an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. 16. Service is carrying out actions taken immediately to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence has occurred against victims.

17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, spiritual guidance for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

3. Regent is the Regent of South Coastal.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of South Coastal Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in the Regional Government of South Coastal Regency.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and increase of women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.

8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and state.

9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).

10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.

11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.

13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Focal Point for Gender Mainstreaming is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.

17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

20. 21. Service is action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
